thread:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Pager:  P99 latency spike + 5xx surge impacting hosted API (route: /v1/generate). Auto-smart-routing fallback triggered. Paging on-call.
incident-bot: Summary: clients seeing ~500 errors and long tails. Traffic being routed from us-east -> fallback eu-west causing cross-region loops. Observed amplified retries.
sanjay: I'm on it. Just pulled traces. Pattern: initial model OOM in us-east queue -> routing policy fails to find same variant -> fallback to eu-west variant -> client retries with standard exponential backoff but short cap -> server side failover also re-routes to eu-west, doubling the inflight requests in eu-west. Hoping this is a retry amplification loop.
maria: @sanjay can you paste a sample trace id? I want to correlate to KV cache hits and model variant metadata.
sanjay: trace: 8a7f3b2c (pasted). Logs show client retry header: `x-retry-count: 3` and our proxy forwards as new requests with `x-routing-fallback: eu-west-v2`.
kevin: Customer impact? Any paying customers seeing errors or degraded latency?
rachel: CS: A small set of enterprise customers reported errors and slow responses in EU during the spike. Patchy but recurring for last 6 mins. I've opened a ticket for the two highest-tier customers and am telling them we're investigating.
maria: Root cause hypothesis: model variant in us-east (redwood-v2-quant) hit transient OOM under a burst; our smart routing policy allows fallback to `redwood-v2-quant-eu`. But because clients use short retry policies, their retries hit the fallback region which in turn triggers more failovers back to fallback when they see high latency, effectively doubling load in eu-west.
tim: If that's true we need an immediate mitigation: 1) stop cross-region fallback for this customer tier; 2) set short-term server-side circuit breaker to return 429 instead of failing over; 3) add a temporary global rate limit for route /v1/generate to reduce amplification.
sanjay: Agreed. I'm going to disable auto-region-fallback for the route and flip a circuit-breaker to prefer `local` only. Applying now.
maria: To disable auto-fallback: run on control plane:
```
# disable region fallback for /v1/generate
redwoodctl policy update --route /v1/generate --smart-routing.enabled=false --rollback-token TMP123
```

sanjay: Applied the toggle at 1769623529. Confirming proxies picked up config.
prod-monitoring-bot: config-update: policy /v1/generate smart-routing.enabled=false applied by sanjay at 1769623529
kevin: Noted. What about client retries? We still have clients hammering eu-west; need to send advisory to SDKs to increase backoff.
rachel: I'll coordinate messaging. Suggest we ask SDK teams to push a small patch to increase base backoff to 300ms and max retries to 2, and to include jitter. I'll draft a short bulletin.
maria: Also enabling server-side 429 on excessive concurrent requests for eu-west pool to break the amplification loop. Command:
```
redwoodctl pool update --region eu-west --route /v1/generate --circuit.concurrency=120 --circuit.response=429
```
sanjay: Executed at 1769623578. Pools are now rejecting beyond threshold with 429.
incident-bot: Metric update: error rate dropping from 12% -> 4% over last 60s. Latency P99 in eu-west trending down.
kevin: Good. Let's keep the fallback disabled until we confirm the us-east model stability and re-run a controlled canary.
maria: Starting canary run of us-east variant with throttled QPS (10% traffic) and monitoring KV cache warmups. If healthy for 5m, we can slowly re-enable fallback with a stricter policy (only degrade to compatible variant not cross-region) and enforce server-side request-header `x-allow-fallback:true` opt-in.
sanjay: Also adding temporary routing rule to prefer same-variant or fail fast:
```
redwoodctl routing rule add --route /v1/generate --rule "prefer_variant_same_region" --on_miss fail_fast
```

tim: Nice. After stabilization we should push a policy change: when a model OOM occurs, mark variant unhealthy for 30s and do not trigger region fallback for the same customer for 60s. That avoids retry amplification loops.
maria: Agreed, postmortem action item.
rachel: Customer comms: sent initial heads-up to affected orgs at 1769623690. Told them we're mitigating and will follow with RCA within 48h.
kevin: Anything left to do for live mitigation?
sanjay: Monitoring continues. I see 429s still coming in but traffic is down 65% on eu-west. I'll keep watching for any flapping.
maria: I'll join the post-incident review and propose these config changes: backoff-safety header (server advertises recommended backoff), disable automatic cross-region fallback by default, and an amplification detector that watches retry headers & increases in a short window.
incident-bot: Incident state: mitigated -> partial (service degraded but fallback loop stopped). Pager cleared for active escalation. Please file postmortem and tag eng-runtime + eng-sre + product.
kevin: Filing the incident doc now.
rachel: I'll follow up with customers with timeline once we have the postmortem draft.
sanjay: Final note: traced one client SDK that did aggressive immediate retries with no jitter. We'll follow up with the SDK team to release a patch and consider server-side protection for older SDKs.
maria: Thanks all. Moving to monitoring-only. Will check back in 30m.
incident-bot: Incident closed for paging at 1769623850 (monitoring watch).
